summary: Full Riftbound test pass: headless tracer invariants + monkey gameplay-flow + per-card playtest on N untested cards. Returns one merged report.
logs: auto-fixing 84 confirmed bugs across 45 files (same-file serialized)

findings.reason: Rule 103.2.b ("Your Main Deck can include up to 3 copies of the same named card") verified via rule.ts. Screenshot 00.png and trace step 5 show player-1's opening hand with 4x Legion Rearguard (player-1-main-3/4/6/10-ogn-010-298), i.e. mainDeckCardIds had >=4 copies. The game-start path never enforces the copy limit: apps/riftbound-app/server/pregame.ts:48-56 (createGameFromDecks) registers every entry of deck.mainDeckCardIds into mainDeck with no validation; apps/riftbound-app/server/decks.ts:126-185 (savedDeckToDeckConfig) expands `quantity` blindly and only checks non-empty/legend/champion; server/routes-deck.ts POST /api/saved-decks stores cards unvalidated, and src/db/schema.ts:72 allows quantity up to 12 in any zone. The engine's copy-limit check (packages/riftbound-engine/src/validators/deck-validators.ts:205-222, MAX_COPIES_PER_NAME=3, via validateDeck at :427) is only ever called from deckbuilder/deck-builder.ts:569 — never from ws-lobby.ts:136-140 / pregame or the riftbound game definition setup. findings.why_wrong: DESIGN.md Board layout: 'Exhausted cards rotate 90° (physical tap) + dark overlay'. The tapped rune should stay inside its stack slot and be dimmed; here it overflows off-screen and is not dimmed, so the exhausted state reads as a hover/selection rather than a tap.

findings.reason: DESIGN.md:12 requires "Exhausted cards rotate 90° + dark overlay". The dark overlay is defined only on `.card--exhausted::before` (css/gameplay.css:315-326), and render/card.js:151-153 pushes both `exhausted` and `card--exhausted` for normal cards. But renderRuneCard (render/runes.js:219) pushes only `exhausted` — never `card--exhausted` — so exhausted runes get the rotation from `.rune-stack .card.exhausted { transform: rotate(90deg) }` (css:518-521) but no dim overlay/lock icon, despite the CSS comment at css:516-517 claiming the overlay applies. The blue border is just the inline calm DOMAIN_COLORS border (runes.js:212,226), so an undimmed rotated rune reads as highlighted. Overflow: the 110x154 card (css:503-508, left:1px) rotated about center becomes 154px wide inside a 112px .rune-stack, protruding ~21px past the stack's left edge; with the rune grid at the viewport's left this clips off-screen. Trace step 10 confirms rune-8 exhausted=true, energy=1.

findings.what: Player clicked 'Recycle Rune' -> 'Calm Rune (2 available)'. The pool held one READY Calm Rune (rune-11) and one EXHAUSTED Calm Rune (rune-8). The UI collapsed both into a single 'Calm Rune (2 available)' button and recycled the READY rune (rune-11), leaving the already-exhausted one in the pool (after: runePool=[rune-8 exhausted], Runes 0/1). The recycle itself resolved correctly (rune deck 10->11, calm power 0->1, energy unchanged, resource bar matches).
findings.why_wrong: Which rune to recycle is the player's choice (rune 'Recycle me: Add [C]' ability is activated on a specific rune object). Grouping by name hides the ready/exhausted distinction and the default picked the strictly worse option: the ready rune could still have been exhausted for +1 energy before/instead of being recycled, so the player silently lost a resource with no way to select the exhausted copy from the action panel. A human would immediately ask 'why did it recycle my untapped rune?'. The sub-menu should either distinguish ready vs exhausted runes or prefer exhausted runes when auto-selecting.
findings.ruleOrCard: Calm Rune (ogn-042-298) recycle ability / rune pool activation choice (rule 143.4-area rune ready/exhausted state matters for [T]: Add [1])

findings.what: After the human (player-1) clicked Pass on the Goldfish's start-of-turn Loose Cannon trigger, the held Turn-2 Beginning phase cascaded Channel→Draw→Main, Goldfish auto-ended, and Turn 3 began. Net result between step 18 and 19: player-1 gained 4 runes (rune pool 1→5, rune deck 11→7) and drew 2 cards (hand 5→7: +Mobilize, +Meditation; main deck 27→25), while player-2 — the Turn Player of turn 2 — channeled 0 runes (rune deck still 12, no runes on board) and drew 0 cards (hand still 4, main deck still 36). Turn 2's Channel and Draw phases were applied to player-1 instead of player-2.
findings.why_wrong: Rule 315.3.b / 315.4.b (515.3/515.4): the *Turn Player* channels 2 runes and draws 1. On turn 2 the turn player was player-2 (state.turn.activePlayer=player-2), so player-2 should have ended its turn with 3 runes (rule 485.7/644.7: second player channels an extra rune in their first Channel Phase) and 5 cards in hand, and player-1 should start turn 3 main with exactly 3 runes (1+2) and 6 cards (5+1). Instead player-1 has 5 runes / 7 cards — a free extra turn's worth of resources — and player-2's 644.7 bonus channel never happened. The flow's channel/draw onBegin use context.getCurrentPlayer() (riftbound-flow.ts) rather than state.turn.activePlayer; when the beginning phase is held for a start-of-turn chain and the *non-turn* player's passChainPriority is the move that resumes the cascade, the flow's current player has evidently diverged to player-1 (the ending-phase code already comments on this exact hazard).
findings.ruleOrCard: 315.3.b, 315.4.b, 485.7/644.7 (Loose Cannon start-of-turn trigger holding Beginning phase)
findings.reason: Trace steps 18→19 verify: player-1 runePool 1→5, player-1 hand 5→7, player-2's hand cards identical (drew 0). Source: channel.onBegin uses `context.getCurrentPlayer()` (riftbound-flow.ts:369) and draw.onBegin likewise (riftbound-flow.ts:422) instead of state.turn.activePlayer (the ending phase at :523-525 explicitly avoids this hazard). The divergence comes from apps/riftbound-app/server/turn.ts:200-206: sandboxAutoPlay, seeing turn.activePlayer===goldfish while the Loose Cannon start-of-turn chain was still active, called preparePlayerRotation (flowManager.setCurrentPlayer(player-1), turn.ts:29-33) then executeMove('endTurn') which fails (turn.ts move condition requires neutral-open, moves/turn.ts:60-64) — and unlike ws-game.ts:96-99 it never restores the current player on failure. So when player-1's passChainPriority resolved the chain, beginning.endIf (riftbound-flow.ts:258-260) released the cascade and Channel/Draw ran for getCurrentPlayer()=player-1 during player-2's turn 2; the goldfish then successfully ended turn and turn 3 channel/draw gave player-1 another 2 runes + 1 card (net +4 runes, +2 cards; player-2 got nothing, no 644.7 bonus).

findings.what: UI shows player-1 at 'Runes 5/5' and rune deck 7 at the start of their second turn (turn 3) with the opponent showing 12 runes in deck and none channeled; no log/indication that the opponent's channel/draw were skipped or redirected.
findings.why_wrong: Consequence of the above, but independently visible: a first-player on their 2nd turn can have at most 4 rune cards channeled total (2+2) per 315.3.b; 5 on board plus 1 previously recycled = 6 channeled is impossible by turn 3. The resource bar faithfully reflects the (wrong) engine state, so this is not a UI desync — flagged only so the observer knows the on-screen counts themselves are illegal.
findings.reason: Rule 315.3.b: turn player channels 2 runes per Channel Phase, so first player at start of turn 3 can have channeled at most 4. Trace: step18 player-1 runePool=1 (after recycling), turn 2 (player-2) held in `beginning` with a start-of-turn trigger chain; step19 (player-1 passes priority) -> turn 3 main with player-1 runePool=5 (all player-1 rune ids: rune-8,7,4,5,0), handCount 5->7, player-2 channeled nothing. Root cause in source: sandboxAutoPlay (apps/riftbound-app/server/turn.ts:200-216) calls preparePlayerRotation(session, goldfish) at line 201, which sets flowManager.setCurrentPlayer(player-1) (turn.ts:32) BEFORE executing endTurn; endTurn's condition rejects while the chain is active (moves/turn.ts:60-64, turnState !== 'neutral-open'), and unlike ws-game.ts:97-98 there is no restore of currentPlayer on failure. So flow currentPlayer stays player-1 during player-2's turn 2. When player-1 passes priority and the chain resolves, beginning.endIf releases and channel.onBegin (riftbound-flow.ts:369-399) uses context.getCurrentPlayer() = player-1, channeling 2 of player-1's runes (and draw at :422/459 draws for player-1). Goldfish then ends turn 2 successfully, turn 3 channels 2 more for player-1 -> 1+2+2 = 5. The on-screen 'Runes 5/5' with opponent 12 in deck / 0 channeled is therefore an illegal engine state per 315.3.b, faithfully rendered by the UI.

findings.what: The step-20 click itself ("Exhaust Rune (5 available)") only expanded a sub-menu and changed no state, which is fine. But the board state it exposes is illegal: player-1 (the FIRST player, active on turns 1 and 3) ended turn 1 with 1 rune on board (step 17/18) and now on turn 3 has 5 ready runes (rune deck 12 -> 7) and hand went 5 -> 7 across the single turn transition (step 18->19, persisting in 20). Meanwhile the opponent (Goldfish, active player of turn 2) still shows Rune deck 12 / Main 36 with 4 cards in hand, i.e. it channeled 0 runes and drew 0 cards on its own turn 2. Net: P1 received 4 channeled runes and 2 draws for one turn; P2 received none.
findings.why_wrong: Rule 430.4.a: a player channels two runes during the Channel Phase of THEIR turn; Draw Phase draws 1 for the turn player (515-517 turn structure; 485.7/644.7 only gives the player going SECOND +1 rune on their first turn, which would benefit P2, not P1). First player on turn 3 who kept 1 rune can have at most 3 runes and 6 cards. The engine appears to have applied turn 2's Channel+Draw to player-1 instead of player-2 (or run P1's channel/draw twice) when the goldfish turn auto-advanced after P1 passed priority on the P2 legend start-of-turn trigger.
findings.ruleOrCard: 430.4.a / 515 (Channel & Draw phase belong to the turn player)
findings.reason: Trace confirms the state: step18 P1 hand 5/runes 1, P2 hand 4; step19 (turn 3 main) P1 hand 7/runes 5, P2 hand still 4 — P1 got both turns' Channel+Draw. Root cause: sandboxAutoPlay (apps/riftbound-app/server/turn.ts:200-205) sees state.turn.activePlayer===goldfish while P2's Beginning phase is held by the start-of-turn legend trigger on the chain, and calls preparePlayerRotation(session, goldfish) (turn.ts:201 -> turn.ts:32 flowManager.setCurrentPlayer(P1)) BEFORE executeMove('endTurn'). endTurn then fails its condition (moves/turn.ts:59-64, chain active => turnState !== 'neutral-open'), but the flow manager's currentPlayer mutation (core flow-manager.ts:979-981, a plain field set outside any move) is never rolled back. When the human passes priority and the chain resolves, beginning.endIf (riftbound-flow.ts:258-261) releases into channel/draw, whose onBegin use context.getCurrentPlayer() (riftbound-flow.ts:369, 422) — now P1 — so P2's turn-2 Channel (2 runes) and Draw (1 card) go to P1. sandboxAutoPlay then ends the goldfish turn for real, giving P1 its own turn-3 channel/draw: net +4 runes, +2 cards for P1, 0 for P2, violating 515.3/515.4 (turn player channels/draws).

findings.what: State visible at step 21 (unchanged by the Recycle-Rune category click, which merely expanded the 'Calm Rune (5 available)' sub-button — that part is fine) shows player-1 on turn 3 with 5 runes on board / rune deck 7 / main deck 25 / 7 cards in hand, while opponent Goldfish still has rune deck 12, 0 runes on board, main deck 36 and the same 4 hand cards it had on turn 1. At end of turn 1 (step 18) player-1 had 1 rune (deck 11) and 5 cards (deck 27). So across opponent's turn 2 + own turn 3, player-1 channeled 4 runes and drew 2 cards, and player-2 channeled 0 and drew 0: turn 2's Channel and Draw phases were applied to player-1 instead of the turn player.
findings.why_wrong: Rule 315.3.b: 'The Turn Player channels 2 runes from their Rune Deck'; rule 315.4.b: 'The Turn Player draws 1'. On turn 2 the turn player was player-2, so player-2 should have 2-3 runes and 5 cards, and player-1 should enter turn 3 with 3 runes (1+2) and 6 cards, not 5 runes and 7 cards. Player-1 is being handed the opponent's resources every turn cycle.
findings.reason: Bug is real, root cause is in the app server, not the engine flow. Trace: step 18 (player-1 End Turn) lands in turn 2 / player-2 / phase "beginning" with player-2's legend start-of-turn trigger on the chain (goldfish already auto-passed; chain.activePlayer=player-1). In that same sandboxAutoPlay pass, apps/riftbound-app/server/turn.ts:200-205 sees state.turn.activePlayer === goldfish and calls preparePlayerRotation(session, goldfish) (turn.ts:29-33 -> flowManager.setCurrentPlayer("player-1")) BEFORE executing endTurn; endTurn then fails its condition (moves/turn.ts:59-63, chain active => turnState != neutral-open), but the flow manager's currentPlayer is left flipped to player-1 (no rollback). At step 19 player-1 passes priority, the chain resolves, Beginning's endIf (riftbound-flow.ts:258-260) releases, and channel.onBegin / draw.onBegin run with context.getCurrentPlayer() (riftbound-flow.ts:369, 422) == player-1, so player-1 channels 2 and draws 1 on player-2's turn. state.turn.activePlayer is still player-2 (only written in turn.onBegin, riftbound-flow.ts:152), so sandboxAutoPlay then ends the goldfish turn successfully and player-1 gets turn 3's channel 2 + draw 1 as well. Net: player-1 1->5 runes, 5->7 hand; player-2 +0/+0 — exactly the trace (steps 18->19). Violates rule 515.3.b/515.4.b (Turn Player channels/draws).

findings.what: Step 22 itself was a harness click-timeout with no state change (energy 0, runes 5/5 ready, no pendingChoice, resource bar consistent), so nothing new broke. But the board it shows is already illegal: player-1 (the FIRST player) is in Turn 3 Main with 5 runes on board (rune deck 12 -> 7) and 7 cards in hand. At end of Turn 1 (step 18) they had 1 rune on board and 5 cards in hand; after passing on the goldfish's start-of-turn trigger (step 19) the game jumped straight to Turn 3 Main with +4 runes and +2 cards, while the opponent (Goldfish, second player) still shows 36 main / 12 rune deck, i.e. it channeled 0 runes and drew 0 cards on its Turn 2.
findings.why_wrong: Rule 430.4.a / 315.3: a player channels exactly two runes in their own Channel Phase, and draws 1 in their own Draw Phase. First player on turn 3 should have 1+2 = 3 runes and 5+1 = 6 cards. The second player should have channeled 3 (2 + first-turn extra, rule 644.7 per digest) on Turn 2. The observed +4 runes/+2 cards for player-1 and +0/+0 for player-2 indicates the goldfish's Turn-2 Channel and Draw phases were applied to player-1 (or player-1's beginning phases ran twice) - a doubled resource curve that a human would spot immediately ('why do I have 5 runes on turn 3?'). Originated at the step 18->19 turn transition, still visible in 21.png/22.png.
findings.ruleOrCard: 430.4.a (Channel two runes per Channel Phase); 515 Draw Phase draw 1; 644.7 second-player extra rune
findings.reason: Trace confirms: step18 p1 runePool=[rune-8], p1 hand 5; step19 p1 runePool has 5 player-1 runes (+4) and hand +2 player-1 cards; p2 hand unchanged (4 cards). Mechanism found in source: at step 18 the goldfish (p2) is in its Turn-2 Beginning phase with its legend start-of-turn trigger on the chain (beginning.endIf holds while chain active, riftbound-flow.ts:258-261). sandboxAutoPlay (server/turn.ts:200-205) sees state.turn.activePlayer===goldfish and calls preparePlayerRotation(session, goldfish), which does flowManager.setCurrentPlayer(player-1) (turn.ts:29-33), then executeMove('endTurn') FAILS because the chain is active (moves/turn.ts:60-64 turnState !== 'neutral-open'). Unlike ws-game.ts:96-98, sandboxAutoPlay has no restore of currentPlayer on failure (turn.ts:206-217 only handles success). So the flow manager's currentPlayer is left as player-1 during p2's turn. When p1 passes priority (step 19) the chain resolves, beginning.endIf passes, and channel/draw onBegin run with context.getCurrentPlayer() = player-1 (riftbound-flow.ts:369, 422): p1 channels 2 (not 3, since firstTurnNumber[p1]!=2) and draws 1. Then goldfish auto-endTurn succeeds and p1's real Turn 3 channels 2 more/draws 1 more => 1+2+2=5 runes, 5+1+1=7 cards, exactly as observed; p2 got 0/0.

findings.what: Step 23's click on 'Recycle Rune (5 available)' only collapsed the rune-action accordion (no state change, resource bar 'Energy 0 Runes 5/5' matches runePools, no pendingChoice) — that part is fine. But the board state it acted on is illegal: on Turn 3 player-1 (who went first) has 5 Calm Runes in play (rune deck 7/12) and 7 cards in hand, while the Goldfish opponent still has 12/12 runes in its rune deck and 36 main + 4 hand = 40 (never channeled or drew). Trace shows the jump happened across steps 18→19 (End Turn → Pass): P1 runePool went 1→5 and P1 hand 5→7 in a single opponent-turn round trip, i.e. turn 2's Channel (2 runes) and Draw (1 card) were credited to player-1 instead of player-2.
findings.why_wrong: Channel phase channels 2 runes for the TURN player from their own rune deck (rule 515 Channel step; 644.7 only grants the second player +1 on their first turn) and Draw phase draws 1 for the turn player. First player on turn 3 after recycling one rune on T1 should have 1+2 = 3 runes and 4+1+1 = 6 cards, not 5 runes / 7 cards; player-2 should have 3 runes and 5 cards. The engine applied the non-active player's beginning-phase gains to player-1 (or ran P1's channel/draw twice), giving P1 free resources every opponent turn.
findings.reason: Trace matches exactly (P1 runePool 1->5 = 1+2+2, hand 5->7 = 5+1+1 across steps 18->19; all 4 new runes are player-1-rune-* ids). Root cause: apps/riftbound-app/server/turn.ts:200-217 (sandboxAutoPlay) calls preparePlayerRotation(session, goldfish) at line 201, which sets flowManager.currentPlayer = player-1 (turn.ts:32) BEFORE trying endTurn; when endTurn fails (turn.ts move condition moves/turn.ts:59-64 rejects because P2's start-of-turn legend trigger left the chain active in the held Beginning phase, riftbound-flow.ts:258-261), there is NO restore of currentPlayer (contrast the human path ws-game.ts:96-99 which does restore). So flow currentPlayer stays player-1 during player-2's turn 2. When P1 then passes priority (step 19), the chain resolves, beginning.endIf fires, and channel/draw onBegin use context.getCurrentPlayer() (riftbound-flow.ts:369, 378-397 channel; :422, 459-464 draw) = player-1, crediting turn 2's 2 runes + 1 draw to P1 from P1's own decks. sandboxAutoPlay then successfully ends the goldfish turn and turn 3 gives P1 another +2/+1, yielding 5 runes / 7 cards while P2 never channeled or drew.

findings.what: Step 25's action itself (exhaust a Calm Rune: energy 0→1, rune-8 exhausted, resource bar 'Energy 1 Runes 4/5', Exhaust count 5→4, Recycle still 5) behaved correctly. But the board state it acted on is illegal and a rules-aware human would spot it instantly in 25.png: on Turn 3, player-1 (who went FIRST) has 5 runes on board (rune deck 7/12) and 7 cards in hand, while the Goldfish opponent has 0 runes (rune deck still 12) and never drew (hand 4, main 36). Trace shows it happened at step 18→19: p2's legend (ogn-251-298) start-of-turn trigger held Turn 2 in the Beginning phase with a chain; when player-1 clicked 'Pass' to resolve it, Turn 2's Channel (2 runes) and Draw (1 card) were credited to player-1 instead of turn player player-2, then the goldfish auto-ended and Turn 3 gave player-1 another 2 runes + 1 card (1→5 runes, 5→7 hand in a single step).
findings.why_wrong: Rule 515.3 / 644: during the Channel phase the TURN PLAYER channels 2 runes from their rune deck (644.7: second player's first turn channels 3 — p2 should have gotten 3, got 0). Rule 515.4: the TURN PLAYER draws 1 in their Draw phase. The non-turn player must never receive the turn player's channel/draw. Likely cause: server/turn.ts preparePlayerRotation sets the FlowManager current player before endTurn, but when the Beginning phase holds on a start-of-turn chain and the opponent's passChainPriority resumes the flow, the channel/draw onBegin callbacks resolve getCurrentPlayer() to the passing player (player-1) rather than state.turn.activePlayer (player-2).
findings.ruleOrCard: 515.3 / 644 (Channel phase — turn player channels 2; 644.7 second player T1 channels 3) and 515.4 (Draw phase — turn player draws 1); triggered via legend ogn-251-298 start-of-turn ability
findings.reason: Trace confirms: step18 turn2/p2/beginning with p2's start-of-turn trigger on chain (passedPlayers=[player-2], priority player-1), player-1 runeCount 1 hand 5; step19 turn3/p1/main runeCount 5 hand 7 (+4 runes, +2 cards in one step = two Channel/Draw phases credited to player-1). Source: sandboxAutoPlay (apps/riftbound-app/server/turn.ts:200-205) sees state.turn.activePlayer===goldfish and unconditionally calls preparePlayerRotation(session, goldfish) → flowManager.setCurrentPlayer(player-1) (turn.ts:29-33) BEFORE trying endTurn; endTurn's condition rejects because the chain is active (moves/turn.ts:59-64, turnState !== 'neutral-open'), and unlike the human path (ws-game.ts:96-98) the goldfish path never restores the flow's current player. findings.expected: A multi-select prompt (0..N units at one battlefield, capped by Might total) both when cast from hand and when played from Hidden
findings.observed: From hand: available moves enumerate only single-target playSpell options (one per unit); multi-target only reachable by hand-crafting the targets array. From Hidden (revealHidden): spell went on chain with no targets, then at resolution a choose-target pendingChoice with remaining:1 appeared; after picking one unit it resolved immediately killing only that unit (no way to pick a second unit even though 2+2=4 was legal, and no way to pick zero).
findings.reason: Fox-Fire (fox-fire.ts) has no hand-authored abilities, so it is parsed at runtime from rulesText. Parser: effects-damage.ts:128 matches "Kill any number of units at a battlefield with total Might 4 or less" but delegates to parseCardTarget (targets.ts:11-52), which only recognizes "all/each" and "up to N" — "any number of" yields no quantity, and the "with total Might 4 or less" clause is dropped (effects-damage.ts:159 only matches ":rb_might: or less"). Verified via bun: parsed effect is {type:"kill", target:{type:"unit", location:"battlefield"}}. Engine from hand: play-spell.ts:318-361 only enumerates multi-target subsets for quantity {upTo:N}; a quantity-less target falls to the else branch (lines 339-361) pushing one Play per single targetId. From Hidden/chain: chain/resolve.ts:92-124 creates a choose-target pendingChoice with hard-coded remaining:1 for any non-"all" unbound target, so only one unit can be picked and zero is not offered. No total-Might cap exists anywhere.

findings.what: "It can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities this turn" is not applied/enforced
findings.expected: After Twilight Shroud resolves on Legion Rearguard, an enemy spell (player-2's Stupefy, 'Give a unit -1 Might this turn') should not be able to choose that unit as its target this turn.
findings.observed: The resolved chain item's effect was only {type:'modify-might', amount:1, duration:'turn'} with no untargetable component; no restriction flag appeared on the unit's meta. Player-2 then cast Stupefy with targets:[player-1-main-1-ogn-010-298]; the engine accepted it (chain-3 targets = the shrouded unit) and on resolution the unit's mightModifier dropped from 1 to 0. Grep shows no engine enforcement of an 'untargetable-by-enemy-spells-abilities' restriction (parser only recognizes the Alpha Wildclaw static form).
findings.reason: Parsing Twilight Shroud's rulesText (ven.json:1174) via riftbound-cards parseAbilities yields only {type:'modify-might', amount:1, target:{unit,friendly}, duration:'turn'} + Flow keyword; the "It can't be chosen by enemy spells and abilities this turn" clause is silently dropped. The only parser recognition of this restriction is the Alpha Wildclaw static regex at riftbound-cards/src/parser/parsers/static-parser.ts:1250-1258 (restriction:'untargetable-by-enemy-spells-abilities'), and grep of riftbound-engine/src for 'untargetable'/'cantBeChosen'/'cannotBeChosen' returns zero hits — no engine code enforces such a restriction during target selection. So an enemy Stupefy can target the shrouded unit.

findings.what: Legion 'When you play me, play two 1-Might Recruit unit tokens here' never fires even when Legion is satisfied
findings.expected: After playing Legion Rearguard from hand earlier the same turn, playing Vanguard Captain to base should put a triggered ability on the chain and create two 1-Might Recruit unit tokens in base
findings.observed: Vanguard Captain entered base (energy 10->7, order 3->2), chain stayed empty, no pendingChoice, base contained only Legion Rearguard + Vanguard Captain — zero Recruit tokens. Root cause: card abilities = [{type:'keyword',keyword:'Legion',effect:create-token}] with no triggered/play-self ability; engine toTriggerableAbilities only walks type==='triggered' and parser KEYWORD_TRIGGER_EVENTS deliberately does not expand Legion, so the 'When you play me' trigger is dropped entirely
findings.reason: vanguard-captain.ts:4-16 has no hand-authored abilities; runtime enrichment (enrich-cards.ts parseAbilities) yields only [{type:"keyword",keyword:"Legion",effect:{type:"create-token",amount:2,location:"here",...}}] (verified by running the parser via bun). trigger-runner.ts:81 toTriggerableAbilities only pushes abilities with a.type==="triggered", and parser keywords.ts:212-219 KEYWORD_TRIGGER_EVENTS explicitly excludes Legion (comment lines 215-218), so no play-self triggered sibling is synthesized. play-unit.ts:393-400 fires play-self/play-card triggers but nothing matches; no other engine path executes a keyword-Legion effect on play. Same defect shape affects ogn-016/020/217/243.

findings.what: 'When you play a token unit, give me +1 Might this turn' never triggers
findings.expected: After Lillia is on board and Desert's Call resolves creating a Sand Soldier unit token for player-1, Lillia's trigger should go on the chain and Lillia should become 5 Might this turn
findings.observed: Sand Soldier token was created in base, but the only chain item was Abandoned Hall's play-spell trigger; Lillia stayed at 4 Might. Parsed trigger event is 'play-token-unit' but the engine never emits that event (create-token handler fires no play/enter events at all)
findings.reason: Parser maps "When you play a token unit" to event 'play-token-unit' (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/trigger-patterns.ts:160). Engine GameEvent union (abilities/game-events.ts:12-38) defines no 'play-token-unit' (nor any token event), and trigger-matcher.ts:161-168 requires exact event-type match. handle_createToken (abilities/effects/create-token.ts:45-65) calls ctx.createCardInZone and sets exhausted/registry but never calls ctx.fireTriggers with any play-card/play-token-unit event. grep for 'play-token'/'token-unit' in riftbound-engine/src returns nothing. So Lillia's trigger can never match.

findings.what: Static 'Your token units have [Tank]' is applied to Lillia herself instead of to token units
findings.expected: Sand Soldier token (and any friendly unit token) gets grantedKeywords Tank; Lillia (non-token) does not
findings.observed: State shows Lillia meta.grantedKeywords=[{duration:'static',keyword:'Tank'}], while the Sand Soldier token has no grantedKeywords (and non-token Legion Rearguard also none). Parsed static is {effect:{type:'grant-keyword',keyword:'Tank',target:{type:'unit',controller:'friendly'}}} with no 'affects' field and no token filter; static-abilities.resolveStaticTargets(undefined) defaults to [self]
findings.reason: Ran parser on Lillia's rulesText: static parses to {type:'static', effect:{type:'grant-keyword',keyword:'Tank',target:{type:'unit',controller:'friendly'}}} — no `affects`, and the "token" qualifier is dropped (effects-grant-keyword.ts:212-231 treats hasMatch[2]='token' only as a tag filter... actually 'Your' branch yields no filter at all in output). enrich-cards.ts:29 registers parser output verbatim. In the engine, static-abilities.ts:542-543 reads `ability.affects` (undefined) and resolveStaticTargets (static-abilities.ts:281-285) maps `undefined` -> [source.id], so Tank is granted to Lillia herself; applyStaticEffect (static-abilities.ts:382-399) never consults effect.target. No token filter exists anywhere in resolveStaticTargets, so Sand Soldier tokens never receive Tank.

findings.what: Tibbers (fury/chaos, power cost 2) cannot be played using fury or chaos power; engine requires literal 'rainbow' power in the pool
findings.expected: Per rule 135.2.e.5.a a [rainbow]/hybrid power pip can be paid with power of any (of the card's) domains; with energy 16, fury 3, chaos 2 in pool, playUnit for Tibbers should be legal
findings.observed: Card is loaded with powerCost ['rainbow','rainbow']; with pool {fury:3, chaos:2, rainbow:0} playUnit is not enumerated and executeMove returns "Move 'playUnit' condition not met". Only playable after addResources {rainbow:2}. canAffordCard in moves/play/cost.ts compares pool.power['rainbow'] >= need literally; recycleRune only ever yields domain-typed power, so all multi-domain cards are unpayable from runes (client auto-pay.js also only special-cases 'all'/'any', not 'rainbow').
findings.reason: Reproduced directly. packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/all-cards.ts:852-861 (derivePowerCost) maps every multi-domain card's power N to N x "rainbow", so Tibbers loads with powerCost ['rainbow','rainbow'] (confirmed via getAllCards()). packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/cost.ts:569-586 (canAffordCard) iterates need-domains and compares `pool.power[domain] >= need` literally — reducePowerCost (operations/static-cost-reduction.ts:288-324) only treats 'rainbow' specially on the *waiver* side, never converts a rainbow *need* into any-domain. deductCost (cost.ts:627-644) likewise subtracts from pool.power['rainbow']. recycleRune (moves/resources.ts:184-212) only ever adds power under the rune's own domain, so pool.power.rainbow is never populated by normal play. Ran canAffordCard with the real loaded Tibbers def and pool {energy:16, power:{fury:3, chaos:2, rainbow:0}} -> false; after setting rainbow:2 -> true. Rule 135.2.e.5.a ("[A] can be paid by Power of any Domain") is honored for ability costs (chain/activate-ability.ts:252, chain/effect-context.ts:105-131) but not in the play-card cost path — a sibling-guard drift.

findings.what: Second ability 'When you move an enemy unit, you may exhaust this to [Stun] it' never triggers / does not exist
findings.expected: After Blast Cone's own play trigger moved an enemy unit (a move I am responsible for — rule 411.4 uses exactly this text as its example), a 'you may exhaust Blast Cone to Stun it' prompt should appear; accepting should exhaust Blast Cone and set stunned on the moved unit
findings.observed: After the enemy unit was moved (twice, in two separate plays) there was no chain item, no pendingChoice, Blast Cone stayed exhausted:false and the moved unit stayed stunned:false. parseAbilities() on the rulesText returns only ONE ability (the play-self move); the second sentence is dropped.
findings.reason: blast-cone.ts:4-15 defines the card with only rulesText and no `abilities` field, so abilities come from enrich-cards.ts:29 calling parseAbilities(rulesText). Running parseAbilities on the exact rulesText (packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/index.ts:42) returns a single ability: {type:"triggered", trigger:{event:"play-self"}, effect:{type:"move", target enemy unit}, optional:true}. The second sentence "When you move an enemy unit, you may exhaust this to [Stun] it" produces no ability (dropped during multi-segment parse / quality comparison at index.ts:181-239). Hence no trigger, no pendingChoice, no stun — matches observed behavior.

findings.what: 'Move an enemy unit' gives no choice of destination — hard-coded to base
findings.expected: Rule 355.4/355.4.a: controller chooses a valid Move Destination (any location other than the unit's current one — base or another battlefield)
findings.observed: Parsed effect is {type:'move', target:{unit,enemy}, to:'base'}; on resolve the chosen enemy unit is always sent to base with no destination prompt. The choose-target options also listed an enemy unit already in base (player-1-main-7), for which 'to base' is not a valid move.
findings.reason: Blast Cone (blast-cone.ts) has no hand-authored abilities so it is enriched via parseAbilities (enrich-cards.ts:29). Running the parser on its rulesText yields {type:'move', target:{type:'unit',controller:'enemy'}, to:'base'} — effects-move.ts:192/224 default `to` to "base" when no destination string is matched (`const to: Location = destStr ? parseLocationString(destStr) : "base"`). In the engine, handle_move (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/move.ts:199-237) only raises a choose-destination prompt when dest === "choose" (line 201); for dest "base" it falls to lines 224-236 and moves every target straight to base with no prompt and no filter excluding units already in base. Rule 355.4 requires the controller to choose a valid destination other than the unit's current location, so the card-layer parse (to:'base' instead of to:'choose') is the bug.

findings.what: Deflect surcharge is charged as Energy instead of Power ([rainbow] = 1 power of any domain)
findings.expected: Opponent choosing Vi with a spell must pay 1 additional Power (any domain); with 0 power in pool the 1-cost Stupefy targeting Vi should be unaffordable / not listed
findings.observed: player-2 (energy 5, power {}) was offered playSpell Stupefy->Vi and it succeeded: energy 5->3 (1 cost + 1 surcharge taken from energy), power unchanged. Engine cost.ts getDeflectSurcharge deducts pool.energy.
findings.reason: Rule 721.1.c/721.1.c.1: Deflect surcharge is Power of any domain. Engine treats it as energy: canAffordCard at cost.ts:588-594 checks `remainingEnergy < deflectCost`, and deductCost at cost.ts:646-648 does `pool.energy = Math.max(0, pool.energy - deflectCost)`. No power check/deduction anywhere for Deflect, so a player with energy but 0 power can target Vi (Deflect) and pays the surcharge from energy, matching the observed 5->3 energy.

findings.what: Deflect surcharge is also applied to Vi's own controller
findings.expected: 'Opponents must pay' — player-1 targeting their own Vi with Discipline (cost 2) should pay exactly 2
findings.observed: player-1 Discipline targeting own Vi: energy 6->3 (3 paid). Control: same Discipline targeting own Legion Rearguard: 7->5 (2 paid). getDeflectSurcharge ignores playerId/controller.
findings.reason: getDeflectSurcharge (cost.ts:277-303) takes `_playerId` but never uses it and never reads the target's owner/controller from state — it sums Deflect values from the registry for every target unconditionally. Both callers (cost.ts:588, 646) add the result to the play cost regardless of whether the caster controls the target. Vi's text (vi-hotheaded.ts:36) is "Opponents must pay", so a controller targeting their own Vi is wrongly surcharged +1.

findings.what: Deathknell — Draw 1 never fires when Watchful Sentry dies
findings.expected: When Sentry is killed, a Deathknell trigger goes on the chain / resolves and controller draws 1 (hand +1, deck -1)
findings.observed: Killed Sentry via Falling Star (3 dmg) and, in a fresh game, via Cull the Weak (kill effect). Both times Sentry moved to trash but no chain item, no pendingChoice, hand stayed 5 and main deck stayed 27. History log shows no draw.
findings.reason: watchful-sentry.ts:7-13 hand-authors `abilities` as a single `{type:"keyword", keyword:"Deathknell", effect:{draw 1}}` entry. Because `abilities` is defined, enrich-cards.ts:22 skips re-parsing rulesText (the parser would have emitted an additional `{type:"triggered", trigger:{event:"die", on:"self"}}` ability). The engine's trigger pipeline only registers `type === "triggered"` abilities (trigger-runner.ts:81 `toTriggerableAbilities`; listener-registry.ts:69) and nothing in riftbound-engine synthesizes a die-trigger from a `keyword: "Deathknell"` ability (grep shows no such handling). Empirically verified with rules-audit helpers: firing a `die` event on a unit with the shipped abilities yields 0 triggers; with the triggered shape yields 1. So Sentry's Deathknell draw never fires, matching the report.

findings.what: Card def declares Deathknell only as {type:'keyword', keyword:'Deathknell', effect} — engine's toTriggerableAbilities only reads type:'triggered' abilities
findings.expected: Ability shape the engine consumes: {type:'triggered', trigger:{event:'die', on:'self'}, effect:{type:'draw',amount:1}} (this is what the parser emits for other Deathknell cards, e.g. Soaring Scout)
findings.observed: watchful-sentry.ts abilities = [{effect:{draw 1}, keyword:'Deathknell', type:'keyword'}] only; no triggered entry. Note: control card Soaring Scout (which does carry the triggered die/self shape) ALSO failed to fire in-app — fireTriggers() only scans base/battlefield/legend/battlefieldRow and handle_kill/SBA move the unit to trash BEFORE emitting 'die', so a self die-trigger can never match (only 'discard' has a just-left-board special case). So both card and engine layers need fixing.
findings.reason: watchful-sentry.ts:7-13 hand-authors abilities = [{type:'keyword', keyword:'Deathknell', effect:{draw 1}}] only. enrich-cards.ts:22 skips the parser when `abilities !== undefined`, so the parser's extra triggered entry is never added (verified: parseAbilities on the same rulesText emits BOTH the keyword entry AND {type:'triggered', trigger:{event:'die', on:'self'}, effect:{draw 1}}). Engine toTriggerableAbilities (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-runner.ts:80-81) only pushes abilities with `a.type === "triggered" && a.trigger`; no keyword->trigger synthesis for Deathknell exists in trigger-runner.ts or listener-registry.ts (despite the header comment). So Watchful Sentry registers zero die-triggers at the card layer.

findings.what: "at the same battlefield" restriction is not enforced (target.location "same" is ignored by the target resolver / play-legality check).
findings.expected: Facebreaker should only be playable when some battlefield holds both a friendly and an enemy unit, and the stunned enemy must share the battlefield of the chosen friendly unit.
findings.observed: With friendly units only at battlefield-player-1-bf-unl-205-219 and the sole enemy unit (dup-...-23) at battlefield-player-2-bf-ogn-276-298, playSpell for Facebreaker was still enumerated; on resolution it stunned friendly player-1-main-7 at bf1 AND enemy dup-...-23 at bf2 (__flags.stunned=true on both). Reproduced twice (hand cast and revealHidden cast).
findings.reason: The target DSL declares `location: "same"` (riftbound-types/src/targeting/riftbound-target-dsl.ts:60) and Facebreaker uses it for the enemy stun (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/facebreaker.ts:27), but the engine never handles it: resolveTarget's location filter (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/target-resolver.ts:135-165) only branches on "here", "base", "move-to-or-from", and "battlefield*"; "same" falls through with no zone filter, so any enemy unit anywhere on the board is a candidate. A grep for "same" across riftbound-engine/src (non-test) finds zero handling in the effect executor or play-spell legality (play-spell.ts:316-331 only special-cases location:"here" for upTo multi-picks). Hence the spell is enumerated whenever any friendly battlefield unit and any enemy unit exist, and the second stun ignores the first target's battlefield — matching the observed cross-battlefield stun.

findings.what: No caster target choice for "Stun a friendly unit and an enemy unit" (rule 355.8 targets chosen on play).
findings.expected: With two legal friendly units (player-1-main-7 and player-1-main-11) at the battlefield, the player should be prompted (per-target playSpell variants or a pendingChoice) to pick which friendly unit and which enemy unit to stun.
findings.observed: Enumerator offered a single playSpell {cardId} with no targets; chain item carried no targets; on resolution engine auto-picked the first friendly unit (main-7) and first enemy with no prompt/pendingChoice at any point.
findings.reason: Facebreaker (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/facebreaker.ts:13-37) is a `sequence` of two `stun` sub-effects with conflicting descriptors (controller:"friendly" location:"battlefield" vs controller:"enemy" location:"same"). In play-spell.ts:252 the enumerator computes `tgt = spellEffect.target ?? refTgt ?? findSequenceLeadTarget(spellEffect)`; targeting.ts:64-84 findSequenceLeadTarget returns undefined when any later sub-target key differs from the lead (line 80: controller friendly != enemy), the fight-pair branch (play-spell.ts:265-291) only applies to `type:"fight"`, so it falls to the else at play-spell.ts:364-369 pushing a single {cardId, playerId} variant with no targets. At resolution, chain/resolve.ts:90-127 only raises a `choose-target` pendingChoice when the top-level `effect.target` exists — a sequence has none — so executeEffect runs handle_sequence (effects/sequence.ts) -> handle_stun (effects/stun.ts:7) -> getTargetIds (_helpers.ts:35-47) -> resolveTarget which slices to the first match (target-resolver.ts:183-184: count defaults to 1). No prompt for either the friendly or enemy pick; first friendly/first enemy auto-selected, matching the observed behavior.

findings.what: Stunned status is not shown in the UI after Facebreaker resolves.
findings.expected: Stunned units should render with the 'stunned' class/marker (card.js checks card.meta.stunned).
findings.observed: Server snapshot sends meta.stunned=false while the real flag lives in meta.__flags.stunned=true (snapshot.ts only lifts 'exhausted' out of __flags). DOM for player-1-main-7 and the enemy dup had classes 'card type-unit exhausted card--exhausted card--summoning-sick' / 'card type-unit card--summoning-sick' — no stunned indicator.
findings.reason: snapshot.ts:373-385 lifts only `__flags.exhausted` into the outgoing meta (`meta: { ...baseMeta, exhausted: exhaustedFromFlags }`); `stunned` is spread from baseMeta which stays at its initial `false` (cards.ts:151). The engine's stun effect (abilities/effects/stun.ts:9,12) calls ctx.counters.setFlag(...,"stunned",true), which core operations-impl.ts:526-532 stores in cardMetas[id].__flags.stunned, never top-level meta.stunned. Facebreaker (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/facebreaker.ts) uses type:"stun" effects, so after resolution the snapshot sends meta.stunned=false and the UI (public/js/gameplay/combat.js:7 checks card.meta?.stunned) renders no stunned marker.

findings.what: "Other friendly units have [Vision]" is granted to Gemcraft Seer itself and not to other friendly units.
findings.expected: Static grant-keyword (target unit, controller friendly, excludeSelf:true) should stamp grantedKeywords Vision on the other friendly units in play (player-1-main-6 and player-1-main-5 Legion Rearguard in base) and not on the Seer.
findings.observed: After playing Seer then two Legion Rearguards to base: Seer meta.grantedKeywords=[{keyword:'Vision',duration:'static'}]; both Legion Rearguards grantedKeywords=None (checked again after a further move/800ms wait).
findings.reason: Parser output for Gemcraft Seer's "Other friendly units have [Vision]" is `{type:"static", effect:{type:"grant-keyword", keyword:"Vision", target:{type:"unit", excludeSelf:true, controller:"friendly"}}}` with no top-level `affects` field (verified by running parseAbilities on the rulesText). The static layer in static-abilities.ts:541-543 resolves targets solely from `ability.affects` (`const { affects } = ability; resolveStaticTargets(affects, card, boardCards)`), and resolveStaticTargets (static-abilities.ts:281-285, 334-336) returns `[source.id]` when affects is undefined/unknown. applyStaticEffect's grant-keyword branch (static-abilities.ts:382-412) never reads `effect.target`, so excludeSelf/controller are ignored and Vision is stamped on the Seer itself instead of the other friendly units — matching the observed behavior.

findings.what: Granted Vision never triggers when another friendly unit is played.
findings.expected: With Gemcraft Seer on board, playing Legion Rearguard should put a Vision look-at-top-card/may-recycle trigger on the chain and then show the reveal-and-pick prompt.
findings.observed: Played player-1-main-6-ogn-010-298 and player-1-main-5-ogn-010-298 to base with Seer in play: no chain item, no pendingChoice, deck order unchanged, log only shows 'dev played Legion Rearguard to base.'
findings.reason: Gemcraft Seer's "Other friendly units have [Vision]" parses to a static grant-keyword that only stamps `grantedKeywords:[{keyword:"Vision"}]` onto target unit meta (abilities/static-abilities.ts:382-411). When a unit is played, play-unit.ts:393 calls fireTriggers → getBoardCards → toTriggerableAbilities (abilities/trigger-runner.ts:72-97), which only reads the card's printed registry abilities of type "triggered"; it never consults meta.grantedKeywords, and no code anywhere in the engine synthesizes a Vision look/recycle trigger from a granted keyword (the only engine references to "Vision" are the inert KEYWORD_DEFINITIONS entry at keywords/keyword-effects.ts:164). Legion Rearguard (ogn-010-298) has only a printed Accelerate keyword ability, so playing it with Seer on board matches zero triggers: no chain item, no pendingChoice. Seer's own Vision works only because the parser emits an explicit play-self triggered ability for the card that prints [Vision].

findings.what: Viktor's triggered ability never fires when controller plays a card on the opponent's turn
findings.expected: After Viktor is on board and player-1 plays Meditation (Reaction spell) during player-2's turn, a triggered ability should go on the chain / a 1-Might Recruit unit token should be created in player-1's base (rule 359.3.e.10: 'when you play a spell' triggers as the spell resolves).
findings.observed: Played Meditation twice during player-2's turn 6 (once in beginning phase in response to p2 legend trigger, once in main phase open state, via REST /move so goldfish auto-end-turn didn't fire). Both times Meditation resolved (drew a card) and Abandoned Hall's 'when a player plays a spell' trigger fired (chain-7/chain-9), proving play-spell/play-card events were emitted, but no Viktor chain item appeared and base still contained only Viktor - no Recruit token. Root cause from source: card def packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/viktor-innovator.ts uses trigger restriction {type:'during-turn', whose:'opponent'}, but riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-matcher.ts restrictionSatisfied() only implements 'on-opponent-turn' (comment references the ven-176-166 printing); 'during-turn' hits the default branch which returns false, so the trigger is always blocked.
findings.reason: viktor-innovator.ts:22 declares restrictions [{type:'during-turn', whose:'opponent'}], but trigger-matcher.ts restrictionSatisfied() (lines 106-147) has no 'during-turn' case; only 'on-opponent-turn' (line 131) is handled and the default branch (line 143-146) returns false, so Viktor's trigger is always blocked.

findings.what: Battlefield-count draw ignores control requirement
findings.expected: With 0 battlefields controlled by player-1 or allies (server state: both battlefields controller:null, turn 1, no units), spell should draw 1 + 0 = 1 card
findings.observed: Hand went 5 -> 8 after resolution: drew 3 (1 + 2), i.e. counted every battlefield in play regardless of controller. Chain effect was {draw 1},{draw amount: count battlefield controller:'friendly-or-allies'} but the controller filter evidently matched uncontrolled battlefields
findings.reason: Parser (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-draw.ts:18-35) emits {type:"draw", amount:{count:{type:"battlefield", controller:"friendly-or-allies"}}}. handle_draw (abilities/effects/draw.ts:10) -> resolveAmount (abilities/effects/_helpers.ts:139-149) -> resolveTarget(target).length. In target-resolver.ts:90-92, `if (target.type === "battlefield") return ctx.zones.getCardsInZone("battlefieldRow")` short-circuits BEFORE the controller filter at lines 125-132, so every battlefield in play is counted regardless of draft.battlefields[id].controller. (Additionally the controller filter only recognizes "friendly"/"enemy", never "friendly-or-allies", and checks card controller not battlefield control.) With 2 uncontrolled battlefields this yields draw 1 + 2 = 3, matching observed 5->8.

findings.what: Reflection tokens do not become copies of Keeper of Masks
findings.expected: After the play trigger resolves, the two Reflection tokens 'become copies of me' — name Keeper of Masks, might 1, Hidden + Temporary keywords and the play trigger (and thus should also die to Temporary at next Beginning Phase)
findings.observed: Tokens created as definitionId 'token-def-reflection', name 'Reflection', might 0, no abilities/keywords (token spec carries keywords:['CopyOnPlay'] but nothing applies it). They survived player-1's next Beginning Phase while the original Keeper was killed by Temporary, confirming they are not copies
findings.reason: keeper-of-masks.ts:16-30 encodes the ability only as create-token {name:'Reflection', might:0, keywords:['CopyOnPlay']} with no copy effect. handle_createToken (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/create-token.ts:31-64) registers tokens under 'token-def-reflection' with the literal name/might/keywords from the spec and never copies the source card. grep for 'CopyOnPlay'/copy semantics across riftbound-engine/src and server.ts returns zero hits — the keyword is inert, so tokens stay 0-might Reflections without Hidden/Temporary.

findings.what: Tokens played 'here' at a battlefield are clipped/invisible in the UI
findings.expected: All 4 friendly units at Abandoned Hall (Reflection, Keeper of Masks, 2 new Reflections) visible in the battlefield zone
findings.observed: The .battlefield container is overflow:hidden (bottom=421px) and the second row of .bf-units renders at y=429-497, so the two newly created Reflection tokens are fully clipped; elementFromPoint at their center returns 'zone-row', and they do not appear in the screenshot
findings.reason: UI layout bug is real in source. gameplay.css:861-874 `.battlefield { ... overflow: hidden; }` clips its content; `.bf-units` (gameplay.css:1082-1093) is `flex-wrap: wrap` with fixed 90x126px cards (gameplay.css:468-472). With `.battlefield max-width:420px` minus `.bf-art` 200px (gameplay.css:877-878) and bf-body/bf-units padding, only ~193px remains, so only 2 cards fit per row; 4 player-side units wrap to a second 126px row. The battlefield's height is bounded by `.battlefield-row` (gameplay.css:109-121, flex:2, min-height:180px inside the fixed 1080px #game-scale-wrapper column), so the wrapped second row overflows and is hidden rather than scrolling/scaling. board.js:106-129 renders exactly this structure (bf-art + bf-body > bf-units player-side). Generic (not card-specific) but matches the observed clipping of the 3rd/4th unit.

findings.what: Play restriction 'Play me only to a battlefield you conquered this turn' is not enforced
findings.expected: With no battlefield conquered this turn, Perched Grimwyrm should have no legal play location (not playable at all); after conquering, only the conquered battlefield should be offered — never base.
findings.observed: Turn 1 with zero conquered battlefields: `pw moves` listed playUnit {location:'base'} and executing it succeeded (energy 8->4, unit landed in base exhausted). After conquering player-1-bf-unl-205-219 the enumerator listed BOTH 'base' and the conquered battlefield as locations. grep shows the card's `PlayOnlyToConqueredBattlefield` static keyword has no engine wiring (card file comment says 'Engine wiring is still pending').
findings.reason: The keyword `PlayOnlyToConqueredBattlefield` is defined only in the card file (/root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/perched-grimwyrm.ts:17, with comment at :11-12 "Engine wiring is still pending") and appears nowhere in riftbound-engine/src or apps/. The playUnit condition in /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/play-unit.ts:58-98 only gates battlefield targets via Ambush, controlled-battlefield (355.2.a), and canPlayToOpenBattlefield; it never consults state.conqueredThisTurn nor rejects base. The enumerator unconditionally offers `location: "base"` (play-unit.ts:220, 283, 306). So the card is playable to base with zero conquests and base remains offered after conquering — restriction unenforced.

findings.what: Crescent Strike deals no damage and never prompts for a battlefield/enemy unit
findings.expected: On play, prompt to choose a battlefield and an enemy unit there; on resolve deal 4 to the chosen unit and 1 to each other enemy unit at that battlefield (here: Eager Drakehound 3-might should die, Legion Rearguard and Demacian Diplomat should each have 1 damage).
findings.observed: With 3 enemy (player-2-controlled) units at Altar to Unity, playSpell paid cost (energy 13->10, mind 1->0), put a chain item with effect {type:'damage', amount:4, target:{type:'unit',controller:'enemy',quantity:'all',location:'here'}} — no pendingChoice, no targets. After both players passed, spell went to trash and all three enemy units still had damage 0, none killed. Log only says 'dev cast Crescent Strike.'
findings.reason: Reproduced end-to-end via createPlayableGame: 3 enemy units at the battlefield, enumerateMoves yields playSpell with NO targets (params {cardId,playerId} only), chain item effect = {type:'damage',amount:4,target:{type:'unit',controller:'enemy',quantity:'all',location:'here'}}, no pendingChoice; after both pass all 3 enemies have damage 0. Root cause (1): card def riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/crescent-strike.ts has no `abilities`, so enrich-cards.ts:31 runs parseAbilities on rulesText, which misparses "Choose a battlefield and an enemy unit there. Deal 4 to that unit and 1 to each other enemy unit there." into a single damage-4/quantity:'all'/location:'here' effect (verified by calling parseAbilities directly) — losing the chosen-unit 4 dmg + 1 splash structure. Root cause (2): play-spell.ts:253-259 treats quantity:'all' as non-caster-chosen so no target/battlefield prompt is enumerated; at resolution effect-context.ts:99 sets sourceZone = getCardZone(spell) = 'chain', and target-resolver.ts:135-143 filters location:'here' to units whose zone === 'chain' → empty set → 0 damage.

findings.what: Crescent Strike effect is mis-parsed as '4 damage to all enemy units here'
findings.expected: Two-part effect: 4 to the chosen enemy unit + 1 to each other enemy unit at the chosen battlefield, with an explicit battlefield+unit choice.
findings.observed: Card def (crescent-strike.ts) has no abilities array; runtime chain effect was a single damage-4/quantity-all/location-'here' effect ('here' is meaningless for a spell), dropping the 'choose' targeting and the 1-damage splash entirely.
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/crescent-strike.ts:4-16 has no `abilities` array, so enrich-cards.ts:29 runs parseAbilities on rulesText at load. Running the parser on the exact rulesText yields a single spell ability: {type:"damage", amount:4, target:{type:"unit", controller:"enemy", quantity:"all", location:"here"}} — no battlefield/unit choice, no 1-damage splash to other enemy units. The bogus location comes from parser/impl/targets.ts:72 (`lower.includes("here")` substring-matches "there"). play-spell.ts:223-225 consumes this parsed ability directly, so runtime deals 4 to all enemy units 'here' as the card claims.

findings.what: Static 'My Might is increased by your points' never applies
findings.expected: With player-1 at 1 VP (after conquering) and later 2 VP (hold), Draven's effective Might should be 3+1=4 then 3+2=5 (staticMightBonus = victoryPoints).
findings.observed: Draven stayed at might 3 with meta.staticMightBonus=0 at both 1 VP and 2 VP (checked via /api/game/:id/state and UI badge). Root cause: static-abilities.ts applyStaticEffect only resolves numeric and {cardsInTrash} amounts; the card's amount {score:"self"} falls through to 0.
findings.reason: static-abilities.ts:353-369 applyStaticEffect for modify-might initializes amount=0 and only sets it for typeof number or an object with "cardsInTrash"; Draven's card def (draven-showboat.ts:15) uses amount {score:"self"}, which matches neither branch, so staticMightBonus += 0. No other score-based amount resolver exists in static-abilities.ts.

findings.what: Optional 'spend 3 XP as an additional cost; if you do, I cost [3] less' is not supported
findings.expected: With player-1 at 4 XP, a playUnit variant with paidAdditionalCost/XP should be enumerated; taking it should deduct 3 XP and charge 3 energy instead of 6.
findings.observed: With xp=4 (via gainXp), pw moves listed only the plain playUnit (no additional-cost variant, unlike Accelerate cards). Forcing playUnit with paidAdditionalCost:true, additionalCostSpec:{xp:3} charged full 6 energy (10->4) and left XP at 4. Parser emits {type:'additional-cost-option', additionalCost:{xp:3}, ifPaid: cost-reduction} correctly, but engine getOptionalPlayCost (moves/play/cost.ts) only recognises energy/power/kill additional costs and ignores xp.
findings.reason: Engine has no XP additional-cost path. getOptionalPlayCost (riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/cost.ts:217-266) only recognises Accelerate, cost.kill, and additional-cost-option with energy/power; the object branch at cost.ts:255-262 reads only obj.energy/obj.power and returns undefined when both are zero, so {xp:3} yields undefined. Consequently play-unit.ts:270-287 (enumerator) never emits a paidAdditionalCost variant, and the reducer at play-unit.ts:329-365 with paidAdditionalCost:true finds optional===undefined, deducts no XP, and applies no ifPaid cost reduction (deductCost at :321 charges full 6). OptionalPlayCost.cost type (cost.ts:202) has no xp field either. Additionally the prebuilt unl.json abilities for unl-178-219 are an empty sequence, so the card is unsupported either way.

findings.what: Invert Timelines resolves with no effect: neither player discards their hand nor draws 4.
findings.expected: On resolution, player-1 (5 cards in hand) and player-2 (4 cards) each discard their entire hand to trash, then each draws 4 (decks 27->23 and 36->32, trash +5/+4).
findings.observed: After both players passed and the spell moved to trash, both hands were unchanged (P1 still Wind Wall x2/Mobilize/Meditation/Legion Rearguard; P2 still its 4 cards), deck counts unchanged (27/36), P1 trash contains only Invert Timelines, no pendingChoice. Chain item effect was {type:'discard', amount:'hand', player:'each', then:{type:'draw',amount:4,player:'each'}}. In engine abilities/effects/discard.ts, resolveAmount('hand') returns 0 (only 'all' is a recognized string) so the loop discards 0 cards; the handler also only acts on ctx.playerId (ignores player:'each') and never executes the `then` draw in the non-pendingChoice branch.
findings.reason: Parser emits {type:'discard', amount:'hand', player:'each', then:{draw 4}} (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-draw.ts:109). In engine, abilities/effects/_helpers.ts:94-96 resolveAmount returns 0 for any string other than "all", so handle_discard (abilities/effects/discard.ts:7) gets count=0; count!==1 so it takes the else branch at discard.ts:26-31 which loops Math.min(0, hand.length)=0 times and never executes `then`. The handler also only reads ctx.playerId's hand (discard.ts:8-10) and no code in riftbound-engine/src handles player:'each' (grep for quoted "each" finds nothing outside tests). Net: spell resolves as a no-op.

findings.what: Repeat cost can be paid multiple times on a spell with a single [Repeat] instance
findings.expected: Per rule 820.1.c.3 ('Each Repeat Cost can be paid only a single time'), Called Shot (one [Repeat] [chaos]) should offer at most repeatCount=1 (base play or play+1 repeat).
findings.observed: With 4 chaos power available, move enumeration offered playSpell with repeatCount 1, 2 and 3 (UI: 'Called Shot (Repeat x1/x2/x3)'). Executing repeatCount:3 was accepted: chaos 4->0 and the chain item became a sequence of four 'look 2' effects.
findings.reason: Rule 820.1.c.3: "Each Repeat Cost can be paid only a single time"; 820.3 allows multiple executions only per distinct Repeat instance. Called Shot has one instance ([Repeat] [chaos]). Engine violates this in three places: (1) play-spell.ts:409-423 enumerator loops `for (let n = 1; ; n++)` bounded only by canAffordCard, not by tiers.length; (2) cost.ts:458-464 and 486-488 deliberately clamp `tiers[Math.min(i, tiers.length - 1)]` with comment "A single-tier Repeat applies its cost to every repeat", so n>tiers.length stays affordable at 1 chaos each; (3) play-spell.ts:72-78 move condition only checks that a repeat cost exists, never that repeatCount <= number of Repeat instances. With 4 chaos power, n=1,2,3 (plus base) are all affordable and accepted, and play-spell.ts:560 executes effect 1+repeatCount times — matching the observed x1/x2/x3 offers and four 'look 2' effects.

findings.what: Otterpus score->draw replacement never applies
findings.expected: With Otterpus on board, when player-1 conquered Abandoned Hall during their second turn (players['player-1'].turnsTaken=2), they should draw 1 instead of scoring 1 point (VP stays 0, hand +1).
findings.observed: victoryPoints went 0->1, hand stayed at 6 cards, deck stayed at 26. No draw occurred. Engine has no checkReplacement call on the score path (replacement-effects.ts declares a 'score' replaces-type but conquer/score-point code never consults it; checkReplacement is only wired for damage/die).
findings.reason: Otterpus (ven.json:1772) parses to a replacement ability with replaces:"score", but the engine never consults replacements on any score path. checkReplacement is only called from abilities/effects/damage.ts:188 and cleanup/state-based-checks.ts:178 (die). The conquer reducer at game-definition/moves/combat/conquer-battlefield.ts:149-153 does `player.victoryPoints += 1` gated only by canPlayerScoreAtBattlefield (operations/scoring-rules.ts:34, battlefield-ability block, no replacement lookup); same direct increments in score-point.ts:160, resolve-full-combat.ts:272, showdown.ts:118, riftbound-flow.ts:331 (hold), abilities/effects/score.ts:10. "score" appears in replacement-effects.ts:38 only as a type union member. So score->draw replacement can never fire.

findings.what: 'pay [1] to draw 1' attach trigger draws for free
findings.expected: When an Equipment is attached to Jax and the player accepts the optional trigger, 1 energy should be deducted and 1 card drawn; prompt should describe the [1] payment.
findings.observed: Chain item effect is just {type:'draw',amount:1, optional:true}; opt-in prompt reads 'Use Jax, Unrelenting ability? Yes/No' with no cost; accepting drew 1 card (hand 5->6 / 7->8) while energy stayed unchanged (8->8) in two separate trials (equipCard path and Weaponmaster-attach path).
findings.reason: jax-unrelenting.ts declares no `abilities`, so enrich-cards.ts parses rulesText. In parser/impl/triggers.ts:82-89 the `^pay ((:rb_energy_N:)+) to ` prefix is matched, sets optional=true, and slices the cost off effectText; payMatch[1] (the cost) is discarded and never attached to the ability. Verified by running parseAbilities on Jax's text: output is {effect:{type:'draw',amount:1}, trigger:{event:'attach-equipment',on:'self'}, optional:true} with no cost field — so the engine resolves a free optional draw and the prompt has no payment to describe.

findings.what: Weaponmaster attaches equipment with a generic cost component for free
findings.expected: Per rule 821.1.c/821.1.c.3, Weaponmaster pays the Equip cost reduced by [A]; Blighted Battleaxe (Equip [1][fury]) should still cost [1] energy when attached via Weaponmaster.
findings.observed: Played Jax with Blighted Battleaxe on board, picked it in the weaponmaster-equip prompt: it attached and energy stayed 8->8 (nothing charged). play-unit.ts comment confirms 'the on-play attach charges nothing'.
findings.reason: pending-choice.ts:242-289 weaponmaster-equip reducer detaches/re-attaches the picked equipment and fires triggers with no cost payment or affordability check at all; play-unit.ts:413-414 comment states "The [rainbow] discount is implicit — the on-play attach charges nothing." Rule 821.1.c requires paying the Equip cost reduced by [A] (821.1.c.3: non-[A] portion still paid), so Blighted Battleaxe ([1][fury], blighted-battleaxe.ts:13) should cost 1 energy but is attached free. Also no 821.1.c.4/.5 can't-pay handling.

findings.what: Picked card is drawn to hand instead of banished and played with -5 cost
findings.expected: Choosing Legion Rearguard (unit) from the top 5 should banish it and play it (cost 2 reduced by 5 -> 0), putting it on the board
findings.observed: pendingChoice was reveal-and-pick with onPicked:'draw'; UI said 'Choose a card to draw'; picked Legion Rearguard went to hand, base stayed empty, energy unchanged (4)
findings.reason: ven-089-166 (Wild Claw) has `abilities:[null]` in riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/ven.json, so all-cards.ts re-parses rulesText. The parser (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-draw.ts:89-95) matches only "Look at the top 5 cards of your Main Deck." and returns `{amount:5, from:"deck", type:"look"}` — dropping the "banish a unit or gear ... and play it, reducing its Energy cost by [5]" clause (verified by running getCardRegistry(): enriched ability is exactly that bare look). In riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/look.ts:41, a look with no `onPicked` and no `then.recycle` defaults to `onPicked = "draw"` (and line 46-47 leaves playEnergyReduction undefined), so the pendingChoice is reveal-and-pick/draw and the pick goes to hand with no cost/board change. Unlike ogn-062-298 Reinforce (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/reinforce.ts sets onPicked:"play", reduceCost:{energy:5}, filter), there is no hand-authored override for ven-089-166.

findings.what: Reveal filter allows any card type
findings.expected: Only units or gear among the top 5 should be selectable
findings.observed: resolvePendingChoice moves offered all 5 revealed cards including spells (Mobilize x2, Meditation, Wind Wall)
findings.reason: ven-089-166 (Wild Claw) has no hand-authored def; it comes from packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/ven.json via all-cards.ts:832/890 and is parser-enriched. parseLookEffect (packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-draw.ts:88-95) only matches "Look at the top 5 cards of your Main Deck." and returns {type:"look",amount:5,from:"deck"} — verified at runtime via getCardRegistry(): the ability effect has no filter, no onPicked:"play", no reduceCost. In the engine, handle_look (packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/look.ts:43,58-60) only sets pendingChoice.filter when effect.filter.excludeCardTypes is present, and defaults onPicked to "draw" (line 41). So the reveal-and-pick choice exposes all 5 revealed cards (spells included) with no type restriction, and picks draw rather than banish+play with -5 cost. The only cards emitting excludeCardTypes are hand-authored ogn/reinforce.ts and ogn/sabotage.ts.

findings.what: No option to decline picking ('You may')
findings.expected: A skip/decline choice so all 5 are recycled
findings.observed: Only 5 resolvePendingChoice moves with pickedCardId; no decline move
findings.reason: ven-089-166 (Wild Claw) has abilities:[null] in ven.json:2749, so enrich-cards re-parses rulesText; parseLookEffect (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-draw.ts:88-95) matches only "Look at the top 5 cards of your Main Deck." and returns {amount:5,from:"deck",type:"look"} — verified by running parseAbilities: no optional/onPicked/reduceCost. handle_look (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/look.ts:40-63) then sets onPicked="draw", onRest="recycle" and only adds optional:true when visionLike||lookEff.optional — neither holds. resolvePendingChoice enumerator (game-definition/moves/pending-choice.ts:220-234) pushes the {accept:false} decline only if choice.optional, so only the 5 pickedCardId moves are offered; the "You may" decline (recycle all 5) is impossible (and the pick draws instead of banish+play at -5).

findings.what: 'Then you may do this: Empower it' clause missing
findings.expected: After playing the chosen unit/gear, an optional prompt to Empower it
findings.observed: No prompt/pendingChoice after pick; chain effect was only {type:'look',amount:5,from:'deck'}
findings.reason: ven-089-166 (Wild Claw) has no hand-authored .ts def; ven.json has abilities:[null], so adaptJsonCard (packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/all-cards.ts:805-807) leaves abilities undefined and enrichCard re-parses rulesText. Running getCardRegistry().get('ven-089-166').abilities yields exactly one ability: {type:'spell',timing:'action',effect:{type:'look',amount:5,from:'deck'}}. parseLookEffect (packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-draw.ts:88-95) matches the un-anchored prefix regex /^Look at the top (\d+) cards? of your (Main Deck|Rune Deck|deck)\.?/i and discards the remainder, so neither the 'banish a unit or gear ... play it' clause nor the 'Then you may do this: Empower it' optional follow-up is emitted. No empower/optional prompt effect exists for this card, matching the observed chain effect.

findings.what: Replacement 'play that token and an additional copy' never applies
findings.expected: With Zilean at a battlefield, playing a token unit (Desert's Call Sand Soldier; Faithful Manufactor Recruit) should offer a 'you may' prompt and, if accepted, create 2 tokens (once per turn)
findings.observed: Zilean at battlefield-player-2-bf-ogn-277-298; Desert's Call resolved -> exactly 1 Sand Soldier token in base, no pendingChoice; then ogn-211-298 ETB -> exactly 1 Recruit token, no prompt. Replacement ability (replaces:'play-token') had no observable effect
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/zilean-time-mage.ts:24 declares `replaces: "play-token"`, but the engine has no such replacement event: /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/replacement-effects.ts:32-40 enumerates ReplacementEvent.type as only "die"|"take-damage"|"move"|"draw"|"discard"|"score"|"enters-ready"|"deals-bonus-damage", and findAllReplacements/checkReplacement (lines 138-139, 265-266) skip any ability whose `replaces !== event.type`. `grep -rn "play-token"` over packages/riftbound-engine/src and apps/riftbound-app/server.ts returns zero hits, so no code path ever raises a play-token event when a token is created — the Zilean ability is dead data and token plays always yield exactly one token with no prompt, matching the observation.

findings.what: 'Kill this: Recycle up to 4 cards from trashes' activated ability can never be activated
findings.expected: With Forge of the Future ready in base (and 1 card in trash), `activateAbility` for the gear should be enumerated; activating should kill (trash) Forge as the cost and prompt to recycle up to 4 cards from trashes
findings.observed: No activateAbility move enumerated for player-1-main-999-ogn-212-298 (trash empty or with 1 card); direct REST activateAbility with abilityIndex 0 and 1 both return CONDITION_FAILED. Root cause in riftbound-engine game-definition/moves/chain/activate-ability.ts: for cost.kill the condition/enumerator do resolveTarget(cost.kill).filter(id => id !== hostCardId) — with kill:"self" this yields [] so the ability is rejected ('host card cannot pay its own kill cost'). This blocks every 'Kill this:' self-sacrifice ability (also gold.ts, divining-shells.ts, poro-snax.ts). Additionally the parsed JSON ability (ogn.json) has cost:{} and an empty effects sequence for this ability, so even the data-layer fallback has no recycle effect.
findings.reason: Card def forge-of-the-future.ts declares the activated ability with `cost: { kill: "self" }`. In activate-ability.ts the condition (lines 453-465) calls `resolveTarget(cost.kill, {...sourceCardId: cardId}).filter(id => id !== cardId)`; target-resolver.ts:80-81 returns `[ctx.sourceCardId]` for the bare string "self", so the filter yields [] and the condition returns false (line 463-464). The enumerator has the identical pattern at lines 674-688 (`.filter(id => id !== entry.hostCardId)` then `continue` on empty). No other branch in the engine handles a self-kill cost (grep for kill across engine shows only these sites plus play-cost paths). So every 'Kill this:' activated ability is unactivatable.

findings.what: Mistfall's triggered ability never fires when a friendly unit is buffed
findings.expected: After Stand United buffed my exhausted Legion Rearguard (with 1 body power floating and Mistfall ready), an optional prompt/chain item to pay [body] + exhaust Mistfall to ready the buffed unit
findings.observed: Legion Rearguard meta.buffed=true after Stand United resolved, but no pendingChoice/opt-in, no Mistfall chain item (only Abandoned Hall's play-spell trigger appeared); Mistfall stayed ready, body power unspent, Legion Rearguard stayed exhausted. Root cause in engine: handle_buff (abilities/effects/buff.ts) only sets the buffed flag; nothing ever calls fireTriggers with type "buff" (grep shows no emitter), so trigger.event="buff" abilities can never match.
findings.reason: packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/buff.ts:7-29 handle_buff only sets the buffed flag/meta and calls checkBecomesMighty; it never calls ctx.fireTriggers({type:"buff",...}). The GameEvent type exists (abilities/game-events.ts:25) and trigger-matcher maps buff->"buff" (trigger-matcher.ts:69), but a repo-wide grep for `type: "buff"` finds no event emitter (only the effect invocation in moves/play/cost.ts:180). Mistfall (riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/mistfall.ts) uses trigger.event="buff", so its ability can never fire.

findings.what: Vex, Mocking's 'When you [Stun] an enemy unit at a battlefield, you may move me to that battlefield' trigger never fires
findings.expected: After Rune Prison / Back Off stunned an enemy unit at battlefield-player-2-bf-ogn-275-298, an optional prompt (opt-in/chain item) to move Vex from base to that battlefield
findings.observed: Enemy Recruit token and enemy Legion Rearguard (dup, owner player-2) both got __flags.stunned=true at the battlefield, but no pendingChoice, no Vex chain item (only Abandoned Hall's play-spell trigger), Vex remained in base. Root cause in engine: handle_stun (abilities/effects/stun.ts) only sets the stunned flag; no code path calls fireTriggers with type "stun", so trigger.event="stun" abilities can never match.
findings.reason: handle_stun at packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/stun.ts:6-15 only calls ctx.counters.setFlag(..., "stunned", true) and never invokes ctx.fireTriggers. Grep for `type: "stun"` across riftbound-engine/src finds only the GameEvent union declaration (abilities/game-events.ts:31); no site constructs/emits a stun event, so trigger-matcher's stun mapping (trigger-matcher.ts:90) can never match and Vex's event:"stun" trigger (riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/vex-mocking.ts:24) never fires.

findings.what: Target for the [Exhaust] ability is chosen at resolution instead of when the ability is put on the chain
findings.expected: Per rule 355.14.b / 355.10.f, the unit target should be chosen as the ability is finalized on the chain (before opponents get priority), so the chain item carries a concrete target
findings.observed: activateAbility with 2 friendly units put chain item {target:{type:'unit'}} with no chosen target and no pendingChoice; the 'Choose a target' prompt (pendingChoice choose-target) only appeared after passChainPriority when the item resolved
findings.reason: activate-ability.ts:819-823 — reducer calls addToChain with { cardId, controller, effect: ability.effect, type: "ability" } and no `targets`; the move params (types/moves.ts:394-411) have no target field and no pendingChoice is raised at activation. Target selection happens only at resolution: resolve.ts:90-125 checks `!boundTargets` and, with >=2 options, sets draft.pendingChoice = { type: "choose-target", ... } when the chain item resolves. This contradicts rule 355.14.b / 355.10.f (targets chosen when the ability is finalized on the chain). Heart of Dark Ice (sfd-052-221) "[Exhaust]: Give a unit +3 Might" goes through this path.

findings.what: Jae's trigger fires when chosen by a non-spell (gear activated ability)
findings.expected: rulesText says 'When you choose me with a spell' — targeting Jae with Heart of Dark Ice's activated ability should NOT draw
findings.observed: Activating Heart of Dark Ice (gear ability) targeting Jae created chain item {triggerEvent:{type:'choose'}, effect:draw 1} and hand went 7->8. Card def jae-medarda.ts trigger is {event:'choose', on:{filter:'self'}} with no spell-source restriction
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/jae-medarda.ts:17-23 declares trigger {event:"choose", on:{cardType:"unit", filter:"self"}} with no spell-source restriction (the doc comment at lines 10-12 even claims a spell filter that is absent). Engine emits the choose event for every resolving chain item regardless of type: game-definition/moves/chain/resolve.ts:136-140 fires {type:"choose", cardId, chooserId} for all boundTargets before checking resolved.type (spell check only at line 149 for play-spell). The GameEvent shape (abilities/game-events.ts:34) carries no source type, so a gear activated ability targeting Jae matches and draws 1.

findings.what: 'When you choose me' trigger is queued after the choosing spell resolves instead of after it is finalized
findings.expected: Per rule 383.4.b.2, targeting-effect triggers go on the chain as pending items right after the targeting spell is finalized, so Jae's draw resolves before Discipline
findings.observed: After playSpell Discipline targets:[Jae], chain held only chain-1 (Discipline) and hand did not change; Jae's draw trigger (chain-2) was only created after Discipline resolved (Jae mightModifier=2 and Discipline's own draw already applied)
findings.reason: The `choose` event (Jae's trigger) is fired only in game-definition/moves/chain/resolve.ts:136-141, inside chain-item resolution right before executeEffect (line 143) — i.e. when Discipline resolves, not when it is finalized. play-spell.ts has no fireTriggers for `choose` at targeting/finalization. So Jae's draw trigger is queued after the choosing spell's effect executes, contrary to rule 383.4.b.2 (trigger goes on chain as pending item after the targeting spell is Finalized).

findings.what: Unit tokens spawned via the sandbox 'Add Token' move (engine move `addToken`, e.g. token-recruit-player-2-27) survive The Ruination's 'Kill all units'.
findings.expected: Rule 185.2.d: a token unit is a unit and is affected by effects that affect units, so every Recruit/Mech token on the board should be killed along with the card units.
