findings.observed: After resolution all card units (friendly, enemy-controlled via transferControl, champion) and an ability-created Recruit token (from Faithful Manufactor) went to trash, but Recruit/Mech tokens created by `addToken` (both player-1 and player-2 owned) stayed in base untouched. Root cause seen in code: moves/token.ts `addToken` registers only `token-def-recruit` in the card registry, not the instance id, so target-resolver's `registry.get(id)?.cardType === 'unit'` filter drops them (abilities/effects/create-token.ts registers the instance id, which is why ability-made tokens die correctly). Reproduced in 3 separate games.
findings.reason: moves/token.ts:131-152 — `addToken` registers only the shared `token-def-<slug>` definitionId in the global card registry and mints instances `token-<slug>-<player>-<n>` via createCardInZone without ever calling `registry.register(cardId, ...)`. abilities/target-resolver.ts:101-105 filters `target.type === "unit"` candidates by `registry.get(id)?.cardType === "unit"` where `id` is the instance card id (registry.get is a plain Map lookup, card-lookup.ts:114-115, no definitionId fallback). So addToken instances resolve to undefined and are dropped from "all units" targeting, surviving The Ruination. By contrast abilities/effects/create-token.ts:58-64 registers each instance tokenId, which is why ability-made tokens die correctly — matching the observed asymmetry.

findings.what: Killed Recruit unit token persists as a card in the trash zone.
findings.expected: Rule 186.1: a token put into a non-board zone ceases to exist immediately; trash should contain only Faithful Manufactor + The Ruination (count 2).
findings.observed: REST state trash = [Faithful Manufactor, token-recruit-1786003589122-0 'Recruit', The Ruination]; UI trash counter shows 3.
findings.reason: handle_kill (kill.ts:9-16) unconditionally does ctx.zones.moveCard({cardId, targetZoneId: "trash"}) for every target with no token check, so a Recruit token (id `token-recruit-<ts>-<n>` minted by create-token.ts:46) lands in trash as a regular card. No rule 186.1 cleanup exists anywhere in the engine: grep for removeCard/deleteCard/cease/isToken across packages/riftbound-engine/src finds only harness/card-state.ts isTokenInstance (used for invariants/snapshots, not removal) and a test-only removeCardFromZone helper. The Ruination ("Kill all units.") routes through this handler, so the killed token persists in trash, matching the observed trash count of 3.

findings.what: Deflect additional cost is charged as Energy instead of Power
findings.expected: Rule 809.1.c: opponent choosing Jhin with a spell must pay 1 Power (of any domain) as a mandatory additional cost; with 0 power in pool the targeting play should be unaffordable
findings.observed: player-2 (energy 14, power {}) was offered and successfully played Discipline targeting Jhin; pool went energy 14 -> 11 (2 for spell + 1 energy Deflect surcharge), power untouched. cost.ts getDeflectSurcharge/deductCost subtracts from pool.energy
findings.reason: cost.ts charges Deflect from energy, not power. canAfford (cost.ts:588-594) checks `remainingEnergy = availableEnergy - adjustedEnergy; if (remainingEnergy < deflectCost) return false` and deductCost (cost.ts:646-649) does `pool.energy = Math.max(0, pool.energy - deflectCost)`. Rule 809.1.c says Deflect costs "an amount of Power equal to [Deflect Value] more ... as an additional cost" and 809.1.c.1 says that Power may be of any Domain. No power-pool check/deduction exists for Deflect, so a player with 0 power and enough energy is allowed to target Jhin (unl-022-219, which has [Deflect]) and pays 1 energy instead of 1 power — matching the observed 14 -> 11 energy.

findings.what: 'When I move, [Add] [1][rainbow]' trigger is placed on the chain with a reaction/priority window
findings.expected: Rule 429.2 / 337.2 and the card's own reminder text: abilities that Add resources resolve immediately on finalize and cannot be reacted to
findings.observed: After standardMove and after gankingMove the add-resource ability sat on the chain (chain item type ability, effect add-resource) and the UI showed 'The Chain — dev has Priority — play a reaction spell or pass'; resources were only added after passChainPriority
findings.reason: Triggered abilities are unconditionally pushed onto the chain in abilities/trigger-runner.ts:455-483 (addToChain with type "ability", triggered: true) with no exemption for add-resource effects; chain/chain-state.ts:203-248 addToChain only fast-paths type "permanent". The only add-resource immediate-resolve carve-out is for activated abilities in game-definition/moves/chain/activate-ability.ts:805-812. standard-move.ts:246 and ganking-move.ts:134 call fireTriggers without resolveInline, so Jhin's "When I move, [Add]" trigger lands on the chain and awaits passChainPriority, violating rules 429.2 / 337.2.

findings.what: Rainbow ([A]) power added by Jhin cannot be spent on a domain-specific power cost
findings.expected: 'When Added to a player's Rune Pool, [A] can be spent to pay a Power cost of any Domain' — with pool {energy:3, rainbow:1} Legion Rearguard's Accelerate ([1][fury]) should be payable
findings.observed: With energy 3 + power {rainbow:1} the enumerator offered no Accelerate variant (it did on turn 1 with fury:1), and forcing playUnit with paidAdditionalCost/additionalCostSpec {energy:1,power:[fury]} played the unit exhausted without spending the rainbow. canAffordCard in moves/play/cost.ts compares pool.power[domain] >= need per domain with no rainbow-in-pool wildcard
findings.reason: Jhin's "[Add] [1][rainbow]" goes through abilities/effects/add-resource.ts:11-14 which stores pool.power["rainbow"] += 1. canAffordCard (game-definition/moves/play/cost.ts:577-586) then checks each needed domain via `pool.power[domain] >= need` with no fallback that lets pool.power.rainbow cover a domain-specific pip (rule 135.2.e.5.b: "When Added to a player's Rune Pool, [A] can be spent to pay a Power cost of any Domain"). deductCost (cost.ts:635-644) likewise only subtracts from pool.power[domain] and clamps at 0, so a forced play never spends the rainbow. The only rainbow handling is on the cost side (rainbow pips in a cost paid from any domain: effect-context.ts canAffordPower, static-cost-reduction.ts reducePowerCost waivers), not rainbow-in-pool as a wildcard. So with pool {energy:3, power:{rainbow:1}}, Accelerate [1][fury] fails the fury check at cost.ts:582-584.

findings.what: Ganking move to an uncontrolled empty battlefield does not contest it / open a showdown
findings.expected: Ganking only adds a destination option to the Standard Move (810.1.b/c); moving to an uncontrolled battlefield should apply Contested and open a Showdown exactly as standardMove did one turn earlier (base -> bf1 opened a showdown with passShowdownFocus)
findings.observed: After gankingMove bf1 -> bf2 (player-2-bf-ogn-277-298, controller null, no units) battlefield state stayed contested:false, interaction.showdown null, no passShowdownFocus move; only conquerBattlefield/endTurn offered
findings.reason: gankingMove reducer (ganking-move.ts:113-138) only exhausts the unit, moves it, and fires a "move" trigger; it has no equivalent of standard-move.ts:261-295 which sets bf.contested/contestedBy and calls startShowdownState when arriving at a battlefield not controlled by the mover. No other engine path applies Contested after a ganking move.

findings.what: Beginning Phase +1 Might trigger resolves as a no-op
findings.expected: At start of player-1's Beginning Phase on turn 3, player-1 controlled 2 runes vs opponent's 3 runes, so Forsaken Baccai should get +1 Might (2 -> 3) this turn.
findings.observed: Trigger item did go on the chain (chain-2, triggerEvent start-of-turn) but its effect is {type:"raw", text:"if you control fewer runes than an opponent, give me +1 :rb_might: this turn."}; after passChainPriority resolved it, Baccai's might stayed 2 (state might:2, meta.buffed:false, card badge shows 2). Condition was met but no might change.
findings.reason: Reproduced: parseTriggeredAbilityInner (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/triggers.ts:44-48) reorders Baccai's text to "At the start of your Beginning Phase, if you control fewer runes than an opponent, give me +1 ...", but condition-parser.ts has no "you control fewer runes than an opponent" pattern, so parseLeadingIfCondition (triggers.ts:121) fails, parseEffects returns nothing, and triggers.ts:189-191 falls back to effect {type:"raw", text:...}. Verified via bun: output effect is {type:"raw"} with trigger beginning-phase. In the engine, executeEffect (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts:138-144) looks up EFFECT_HANDLERS[effect.type]; there is no "raw" handler (effects/index.ts:58ff), so it hits the explicit "default: no-op" branch. Hence the trigger goes on the chain and resolves with no might change.

findings.what: 'At the start of your Main Phase' trigger never fires
findings.expected: With Bottled Constellation plus 3 other friendly units (3x Legion Rearguard) in base, at the start of player-1's Main Phase on turn 3 an optional prompt/chain item should appear offering to kill 3 other friendly units/gear to score 1 point.
findings.observed: Turn 3 reached Main Phase with no chain item, no pendingChoice, no log entry; VP stayed 0, all 3 Rearguards alive. Engine has no 'main-phase' GameEvent (trigger-matcher EVENT_MAP has start-of-turn/end-of-turn only; beginning-phase is aliased but main-phase is not), and the parsed effect is type 'raw' ("kill 3 other friendly units and/or gear to score 1 point.") so it would be a no-op even if it fired.
findings.reason: riftbound-flow.ts:486-494 main phase onBegin only sets turn.phase="main" and never calls fireTriggers (start-of-turn fired at :314, end-of-turn at :527, nothing for main). trigger-matcher.ts:66-93 EVENT_MAP has no "main-phase"; :164-166 aliases only "beginning-phase"->"start-of-turn". Parser emits event "main-phase" (trigger-patterns.ts:363) but engine never fires it. Card def ven.json ven-067-166 has abilities: [] / parseSuccess: false, so nothing would run even if fired.

findings.what: The +2 [Might] granted by Kha'Zix's attack trigger is not used in combat damage resolution
findings.expected: Kha'Zix (4 base, +2 this turn = 6, shown as 6 in UI and meta.mightModifier=2) attacking a lone 5-Might Playful Phantom should deal 6 (kill Phantom), take 5 (<6, survive) and conquer the battlefield
findings.observed: After resolveFullCombat Kha'Zix was killed (moved to trash) and the 5-Might Phantom survived undamaged; battlefield stayed uncontrolled, no VP. Outcome matches combat computed with base might 4 (resolve-full-combat.ts builds CombatUnit.baseMight from registry def.might and never adds meta.mightModifier)
findings.reason: resolve-full-combat.ts:116 sets `const baseMight = def?.might ?? 0;` from the static registry definition and builds CombatUnit at :149-156 with only that value; `meta.mightModifier` is read nowhere in the move (only reset to 0 on kill at :214). combat-resolver.ts:74 (lethalThreshold) and :89 (calculateSideMight) use `unit.baseMight` plus Assault/Shield keyword values only. So Kha'Zix's +2 (stored as meta.mightModifier=2) never reaches damage dealt or survival threshold: attacker total = 4 vs Phantom 5 -> Kha'Zix (threshold 4) dies to 5, Phantom (threshold 5) survives 4, matching the observed outcome.

findings.what: Conscription resolves with no effect at all — no target selection, no take-control/exhaust/recall
findings.expected: On play, prompt to choose an enemy unit at a battlefield with 3 Might or less (only the 1-Might Watchful Sentry at Back-Alley Bar was legal; 5-Might Phantom at Abandoned Hall and the enemy Sentry in base should be excluded); on resolution that unit becomes controlled by player-1, is exhausted, and is recalled to player-1's base
findings.observed: playSpell put a chain item with no effect/targets ({cardId,controller,resolveTo:trash,type:spell}); no pendingChoice or per-target move; after passing priority the spell went to trash and all three enemy units were unchanged (owner/controller player-2, ready, same zones). Runtime parser output for this rulesText is only [{type:'static',effect:{type:'additional-cost-option',additionalCost:{xp:5},optional:true}}] — the entire 'Choose an enemy unit… Take control of it, exhaust it, and recall it' sentence is dropped
findings.reason: conscription.ts:4-16 declares no `abilities`, so enrich-cards.ts:29 falls back to parseAbilities(rulesText). Running the parser on this exact rulesText yields only [{type:'static',effect:{type:'additional-cost-option',additionalCost:{xp:5},optional:true}}] — no `spell`-type ability; the 'Choose an enemy unit… Take control of it, exhaust it, and recall it' sentence is dropped. play-spell.ts:135/553 and chain/resolve.ts:58 look up `abilities.find(a => a.type === "spell")`, find nothing, so the chain item has no effect/targets and the spell resolves to trash with no state change. Matches observed behavior.

findings.what: Optional 'spend 5 XP as an additional cost' is never offered
findings.expected: With player-1 at 6 XP, playing Conscription should offer paying 5 XP (e.g. a paidAdditionalCost playSpell variant or a pendingChoice), deduct 5 XP if taken, and widen targeting to any enemy unit at a battlefield (the 5-Might Phantom)
findings.observed: With xp=6 `moves` listed a single playSpell variant {cardId,playerId} (no additionalCostSpec/paidAdditionalCost like Accelerate units get); no prompt appeared on play; XP stayed 6 after resolution
findings.reason: Card def /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/conscription.ts:4-16 has no `abilities` array at all (rulesText only). Independently, even a parsed `{additionalCost:{xp:5}}` would be dropped: getOptionalPlayCost in riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/play/cost.ts:245-262 only decodes energy/power and returns kind:"pay" only when `energy > 0 || power.length > 0` (line 260), so an XP-only cost yields undefined; play-spell.ts:376-397 only enumerates the paidAdditionalCost variant when optionalPay?.kind === "pay". No xp deduction path exists in play/*.ts. Hence no paid variant, no prompt, XP unchanged.

findings.what: Deflect on the Bird token is charged as +1 ENERGY instead of 1 power of any domain ([rainbow]), so an opponent with zero power can still target it.
findings.expected: Per reminder text 'Opponents must pay [rainbow] to choose it with a spell or ability' (rainbow = power of any domain, rule 135.2.e.5): player-2 with 11 energy / 0 power should be unable to target the Bird with Moonlight Affliction (or must pay 1 power).
findings.observed: player-2 (energy 11, power {}) successfully cast Moonlight Affliction (cost 7) targeting token-bird; energy went 11 -> 3 (7 + 1 energy surcharge), power untouched. Engine code confirms: cost.ts deductCost/canAfford apply getDeflectSurcharge to pool.energy (and getDeflectSurcharge ignores playerId, so it would also surcharge the controller's own targeting).
findings.reason: Rule 721 (Deflect): "Spells and abilities an opponent controls that choose me cost [X] Power more as an additional cost" — Power of any domain. Engine charges it as energy instead: cost.ts:588-594 (canAfford) checks `remainingEnergy < deflectCost` against availableEnergy, and cost.ts:646-649 (deductCost) does `pool.energy = Math.max(0, pool.energy - deflectCost)`; pool.power is never checked or debited for Deflect. So a player with 0 power and enough energy passes canAfford and pays energy, matching the observed 11 -> 3 (7 + 1). Additionally getDeflectSurcharge (cost.ts:277-303) ignores _playerId/_state, so it never checks that the caster is an opponent of the target's controller.

findings.what: 'spend a buff' cost is never paid — engine has no handler for effect type 'spend-buff' (EFFECT_HANDLERS in packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/index.ts), so it silently no-ops
findings.expected: Accepting the trigger with a buffed friendly Legion Rearguard on board should remove Rearguard's buff (702.2.b), then buff Wildclaw Shaman (+1 Might -> 4) and ready it
findings.observed: After accept: Legion Rearguard still buffed:true (might badge 3), Wildclaw Shaman buffed:false / might 3. No prompt to pick which buff to spend.
findings.reason: The OGN card def (packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/ogn/wildclaw-shaman.ts) has no explicit `abilities`, so enrich-cards.ts runs parseAbilities on rulesText at load; running the parser yields sequence[{type:"spend-buff", then:{type:"buff",target:"self"}}, {type:"ready",target:"self"}] (parser/impl/effects-might.ts:265 emits type "spend-buff"). EFFECT_HANDLERS in packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/index.ts:58-113 has no "spend-buff" key (grep finds zero matches in riftbound-engine/src), and effect-executor.ts:139-144 does `const fn = EFFECT_HANDLERS[effect.type]; if (fn) {...} else { // default: no-op }`. So the spend-buff cost (and its nested `then: buff self`) silently no-ops — no buff is removed from Rearguard and Shaman is not buffed, matching the observed behavior.

findings.what: 'ready me' resolves unconditionally, even when no buff was/could be spent
findings.expected: 'spend a buff to buff me and ready me' — both buff and ready are gated on paying the spend-a-buff cost; with zero buffs on board (or when the cost isn't paid) Shaman should stay exhausted
findings.observed: With no buffed unit anywhere, play Shaman -> opt-in Yes -> Shaman exhausted:true became exhausted:false (free ready, might unchanged 3). Parsed effect is sequence[{spend-buff, then: buff self}, {ready self}] — ready sits outside the cost gate.
findings.reason: Parser (riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-might.ts:255-265 + sequence splitting) yields sequence[{type:"spend-buff", then:{buff self}}, {type:"ready", target:self}] for ogn-147-298 (verified by running parseAbilities on the rulesText; enrich-cards.ts:29 uses this at load). In the engine, EFFECT_HANDLERS (riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/index.ts:58-113) has no "spend-buff" entry, so executeEffect (effect-executor.ts:139-144) no-ops it — no cost is paid and nothing gates. handle_sequence (effects/sequence.ts:21-43) then executes every sub-effect unconditionally, so "ready self" resolves even with zero buffs on board. Ready sits outside the spend-buff cost gate exactly as reported.

findings.what: Opt-in prompt offered when cost is unpayable
findings.expected: With no friendly buffed unit, the 'you may spend a buff' option should not be offered (or accepting should do nothing)
findings.observed: 'Use Wildclaw Shaman ability? Yes/No' modal shown with zero buffs on board; Yes produced a free ready
findings.reason: Wildclaw Shaman has no hand-authored abilities, so enrich-cards.ts:29 uses the parser, which yields optional triggered effect = sequence[ {type:"spend-buff", then: buff self}, {type:"ready", target:self} ]. (1) packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain/resolve.ts:41-48 unconditionally sets pendingChoice {type:"opt-in"} for any `optional` chain item with no cost/payability check — so the Yes/No modal shows with zero buffs on board. (2) The engine has no "spend-buff" handler: packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/index.ts registers "spend-xp" (line 108) but nothing for spend-buff, and effect-executor.ts:139-144 no-ops unknown effect types. The sequence then proceeds to the sibling "ready self" effect, producing a free ready. (Parser also mis-scopes: ready is outside the spend-buff `then`, packages/riftbound-cards/src/parser/impl/effects-might.ts:256-265.)

findings.what: 'draw 1 or buff me' mode choice is never presented; engine auto-picks the first option (draw)
findings.expected: After opting in, player should be prompted to choose between 'draw 1' and 'buff me'; choosing buff should set Buhru Captain buffed (+1 Might -> 4)
findings.observed: Opt-in Yes immediately drew a card (hand 5->6), pendingChoice null, Buhru might 3/buffed:false. No mode-selection prompt in moves or UI. handle_choice in packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/choice.ts hardcodes options[0] ('pick the first option for now').
findings.reason: packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effects/choice.ts:7-10 — handle_choice comments "pick the first option for now (needs UI input)" and calls executeEffect(options[0].effect, ctx) unconditionally. Buhru Captain's rulesText parses to a triggered optional ability with effect {type:"choice", options:[draw 1, buff self]} (verified via parseAbilities). grep across riftbound-engine/src (non-test) shows no code constructs a pendingChoice of type "choose-mode" — only the resolver (game-definition/moves/pending-choice.ts:307) and harness consume it; tests inject it manually (decisions.test.ts:344). So after opt-in, the draw mode always executes and no mode prompt is presented.

findings.expected: With my only unit at a battlefield I control, Arcane Shift banishes it, the pending replay keeps the chain/closed state alive so the battlefield stays controlled, and on finalize I may replay the unit to that same battlefield (only base or battlefields I control are legal destinations; an uncontrolled battlefield is not). The 'Deal 3' hits an enemy unit; the replayed unit survives at the controlled battlefield.
findings.observed: Core control-retention works: after Arcane Shift resolved, Legion Rearguard sat in banishment with a pending 'move to:choose' chain item, battlefield player-1-bf-unl-205-219 stayed controller=player-1 throughout, and the choose-destination prompt offered that battlefield; picking it put the unit back there with control intact. Divergences: (1) the destination options were ['base', my controlled BF, AND battlefield-player-2-bf-ogn-277-298 which I do not control and which holds an enemy unit] -- contradicts 'as long as you control the battlefield' / attackers cannot replay to an uncontrolled battlefield. (2) The legal playSpell move enumerated only one target (the friendly unit); on resolution the 'Deal 3' was applied to the banished friendly unit (dmg=3 in banishment, enemy dup dmg=0), the damage persisted through banish->replay, and once the chain emptied the 2-might unit died to trash and the battlefield became uncontrolled -- so the net outcome of 'replay it there' fails. (Passing two targets [friendly, enemy] instead banished BOTH units and dealt 3 to both.) (3) Arcane Shift went to trash rather than banishment despite 'Banish this'.
findings.notes: Setup: goldfish, tutored sfd-200-221 + ogn-010-298, played Legion Rearguard to base, readyCard, standardMove to own bf, passed showdown to conquer (controller=player-1), duplicateCard enemy Legion Rearguard at the other bf, then playSpell Arcane Shift -> passChainPriority -> resolvePendingChoice(pickedZoneId=own bf). The specific rule interaction the FAQ explains (323.6 cleanup step 4 suppressed while chain pending, 355.2 choose location) MATCHES; verdict is DIVERGES because the destination filter admits uncontrolled battlefields and the effect-step targeting misroutes the 3 damage onto the replayed unit so it dies after cleanup. Screenshots: /tmp/ruling-ee735b43996dcbd3-choice.png (destination prompt), /tmp/ruling-ee735b43996dcbd3.png (final). Note: first attempt was lost to a dev-server restart mid-run (Game not found); rerun succeeded.
